It's possession by Jesus. When you partake in Jesus, you become a part of him and must obey exactly what he wants. This is confusing because it's cannibalism, but among the Greek mystery cults, eating food means consuming Dianesis’s energy. They tear people apart to replicate the death of Dianis and consume body parts.

These mystery cults are demonic, with ritual sacrifices where they tear a person's body apart, replicating the death of Dianis and consuming body parts. This tradition dates back 15,000 years in Europe during the Magdalinian age, where cannibalism was common for religious purposes. Consuming someone’s body after their death would ensure eternal communion with them.

During the Eucharist, you become completely possessed by Jesus, losing your individuality and freedom. Paul's followers might have thought this disobeyed Jesus' teachings, but he built a blueprint for an empire. Romans forced this religion on everyone, making it hard to convince many people otherwise, as most were born into believing these doctrines.

Throughout history, including the Aztecs and Magnolian culture, cannibalism was common, often used to prepare for war or strengthen group cohesion during the ice age. While not everyone practiced it, its prevalence explains why this practice persisted.
